notes:
Summary: mid-market fintech building sub-100ms user-facing trading alerts and high-throughput reranking for market signals. Very cost-sensitive; target unit economics key to go/no-go. Prefer private/VPC deployment with strict residency and KMS controls. Interested in Redwood's Dedicated for predictable throughput and Optimize recommendations to push down per-token cost.

Recent activity timeline:
- 2024-10-03: Intro call (Maya) — high level infra and compliance. Client: 'we cannot lose trades to inference lag' — emphasized p99 and p95 targets.
- 2024-10-17: Technical deep-dive (Ravi + infra) — shared request patterns (bursty market-open spikes ~400 req/s for 30s), average live message length ~120 tokens, typical session TTL short. Added to Drive: request-patterns.csv. (ff_20241017_2210)
- 2024-10-25: Security screen — Glasswater asked for SOC2 + audit logging examples; legal asked about data residency; submitted Security-FAQ.pdf. Ticket created INF-2319.
- 2024-11-05: Kickoff POC (2-week perf) with Redwood Dedicated in eu-west for NA customers via VPC peering test. POC tasks: baseline latency, dynamic batching, KV prefix caching, INT8 quantization run. (ff_20241105_8345)
- 2024-11-12: Mid-POC sync — preliminary numbers: p50 ~28ms, p95 ~120ms on default config; optimized batch + cache run achieved p95 ~68ms but introduced 0.9% classification drift on reranker scores (client flagged). Shared results sheet in Drive.

Use-case & technical requirements (what they told us):
- workload: real-time trading signal scoring + reranking (tight correctness requirements), secondary stream: market-summary generation for live dashboards.
- latency targets: p95 < 80ms for reranker inference; soft p95 < 150ms for summarization. p99 budget subject to canaries.
- throughput: baseline sustained 150–250 req/s, spikes to 400–600 req/s for 15–45s at market open/close.
- cost sensitivity: ops wants per-request cost to be < $0.002 (target), total ARR constraints. Looking for batching/caching/quantization levers to meet cost target without degrading rerank accuracy.
- model preferences: open-chat/decoder variants allowed; will evaluate quantized Llama-2-chat and Vicuna derivatives. Must support fallbacks to smaller models during degraded capacity.
- routing & fallback: route by latency region; automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants acceptable if accuracy delta quantified.

POC focus and experiments run in POC:
- continuous batching policy (adaptive batch size tied to latency SLO), measurement of tail vs avg latency.
- prefix/KV caching for recurring instrument context (expected hit rate ~23%).
- INT8 + mixed-precision quantization to reduce memory footprint on dedicated GPUs; compare quality on reranker metrics (MRR, precision@5).
- benchmarking harness: reproducible perf plan (scripts in Drive), trace IDs attached, and per-route cost calc sheet.

Key quotes / customer color:
- 'If we can't hold p95 under ~80ms without >1% drop in accuracy we won't move forward.' — Head of ML Ops (A. Kumar).
- Procurement: 'Need SOW + clear indemnities; procurement freeze likely until Jan.'

- Redwood to provide detailed batching/caching config examples and expected unit-cost impact (Optimize output).
- Security: provide live audit log sample and KMS keyflow diagram (Ravi -> Sec team).
- Commercial: prepare SOW v1 with 3-month ramp pricing; finance to confirm ARR band.

Blockers / risks:

- Quantization causing small but non-negligible score drift on the reranker — customer wants guarantees/thresholds.
- Data residency and SOC2 gap items outstanding; legal requests more artifacts.

Attachments & links: pricing deck and perf sheet in Drive; Fireflies transcripts for 10/17 and 11/05. Gmail thread references for SOW negotiations. Jira tickets INF-2319 (perf), SEC-4021 (security).

Highly likely to convert if we can: a) demonstrate quantization profile with <0.5% MRR impact, b) accept VPC deployment + KMS, c) propose commercial ramp that smooths traffic cost at market spikes. Procurement timeline is the gating factor.
